## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`list_orders` should accept and forward an offset, because as written the order listing can only ever return its first page. The `limit=0` boundary of the new validation also has no test.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/paging.py` with a `paginate(items, limit, offset=0)` slicing helper that rejects negative arguments. It gives `list_orders` an optional `limit` that it passes to that helper after sorting newest first, and adds tests for both.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/orders.py:9 — correctness — Expose offset in list_orders so later pages are reachable — With five orders, `list_orders(orders, limit=2)` always returns the two newest, and no argument returns the other three. `list_orders` accepts only `limit` and calls `paginate(ordered, limit)`, so `offset` is always 0. — Callers of the order listing cannot fetch any page after the first, so the pagination the title names is not delivered. — Fix: Add an `offset=0` parameter, call `paginate(ordered, limit, offset)`, and extend `test_limit_caps_results` in `tests/test_orders.py`.

## Suggestions
- app/paging.py:9 — tests — Add a test for limit=0 returning an empty page — `paginate([1, 2, 3], limit=0)` returns `[]`, but no test calls it. The added tests use limits of -1, 2 and `None`, so changing `limit < 0` to `limit <= 0` would make a zero limit raise with every test still passing. — A later change to the validation boundary can turn a zero limit into an error without any test failing.

## Not reviewed
- The text of issue #12 in this repository's issue tracker, which the pull-request body says this change closes, was not available to confirm the requested pagination behaviour.
